ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Objects A and B start moving from the same place in the same direction. The relationship between their velocities and time is as shown in the figure. In the figure, $t_2=\frac{t_4}{2}$, and both curve segments are 1/4 circular arcs. At what moment are the two objects farthest apart?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Description of the image: In the attached v-t graph, the horizontal axis is time t, the vertical axis is velocity v, and the lower left is O. There is a horizontal dashed line v0 on the graph, and vertical dashed lines mark t1, t2, t3, and t4. The velocity graph marked “A” is a broken line: it rises in a straight line from O to (t2, v0), then descends in a straight line to (t4, 0). The velocity graph marked “B” consists of two 1/4 circular arcs: the first segment descends from (0, v0) to (t2, 0), and the second segment rises from (t2, 0) to (t4, v0). The graphs of A and B intersect at t1 and t3 respectively, and the problem gives t2=t4/2, so the two time intervals [0,t2] and [t2,t4] have equal widths. Reasoning: The two objects start from the same place and move in the same direction, so their relative displacement is equal to the signed area between the two velocity curves in the v-t graph, namely Δx=∫(vA-vB)dt. The candidate moments when they are farthest apart should occur where the relative velocity is zero, that is, at t1 and t3 where the two velocity graphs intersect, and the endpoints also need to be checked. First look at the endpoint t4: the area under A's velocity graph is the area of a triangle with base t4 and height v0, namely 1/2·t4·v0=t2v0. The area of B's left circular-arc segment and the area of its right circular-arc segment are complementary within two equal-width regions: the left segment is equivalent to the rectangle t2v0 minus a 1/4 circle area, and the right segment is equivalent to a 1/4 circle area of the same size, so B's total area from 0 to t4 is also t2v0. Therefore, at t4 the total displacements of the two objects are equal, and the distance is 0. From 0 to t1, B's velocity in the graph is greater than A's, and the magnitude of the distance at t1 is equal to the small area difference between 0 and t1; from t3 to t4, B's velocity is again greater than A's, and since the total distance returns to 0 at t4, the magnitude of the distance at t3 is equal to the remaining area difference between t3 and t4. Comparing these two circular-arc area blocks in the graph, the area block from t3 to t4 is clearly greater than the area block from 0 to t1; if calculated after normalization, the area at t1 is also (4-π)/8·t2v0, while the area at t3 is π/8·t2v0, and the latter is greater. Therefore, the two objects are farthest apart at t3.
